newsitem.title: USA: Visa says costs of new liabiility program "small".
newsitem.headline: Visa says costs of new liabiility program "small".

text.p: Visa U.S.A. said Wednesday the cost of its new policies on liability for lost and stolen credit and debit cards would be absorbed by member banks but the risk is "very small."

"The risk actually is very small ... and it's going to be absorbed by the banks," said Carl Pascarella, president and chief executive of Visa U.S.A., in a telephone conference call with reporters. Without disclosing any figures, he said the costs were "clearly within the comfort level of both ourselves and the member banks."
Pascarella said fraud losses have amounted to less than one tenth of one percent of annual card volume.
Purchases of goods and services with Visa cards worldwide totaled $1 trillion in the 12 months ended March 31.
Annual U.S. volume is more than $460 billion including about $63 billion spent on check cards, also known as debit cards.

Pascarella said the check cards are growing rapidly and should account for 20 percent of U.S volume in 1998. Presently there are 46 million Visa check cards in the U.S. amounting to 80 percent of the check card market.

Earlier Wednesday, Visa U.S.A. said holders of U.S. credit and check cards would be subject to zero liability if loss, theft or unauthorized use of cards was reported in two business days. After the initial period, consumers would have a maximum liability of $50.
Visa also announced members would extend provisional credit within five days of notification for lost funds due to unauthorized transactions.
Further, any unsolicted check cards sent to consumers will have to be personally activiated before they can be used.

In a statement, MasterCard International, a competing card group, said it has the leadership role in providing enhanced protection to holders of debit cards. Further details were not immediately available.
